# `chk_lia_f1` — VF4 over the F1 corpus

`docs/DECISIONS.md` R162. The fixture family compiles the theory `theories/chk_lia`
(its `ORDER`'s `theory chk_lia` line) and then `ChkLIAF1.lean`, which
`scripts/vf4_chk_lia_corpus.py` GENERATES (a hand edit is drift; `--check` exits 1
on it) from `reports/2026-10-26-vf4-f1-corpus/harvest.ndjson`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ChkLIAF1.lean` | one theorem per distinct certified obligation: `chk_LIA_cases [(case, certificate), …] = true := rfl` |
| `corpus.tsv` | every harvested obligation: its VF3 census row (test, revision, function), source (`safety` or `r1-site:<callee>`), kind and location, what the compiler said, and the producer's outcome |

**The corpus.** Every obligation of every VF3-census row
(`docs/trust-core/denominators/vf3-proved-census.tsv` at Trust `6af3d62c55f`,
measured at `fa054122ff0`) whose fragment or body fragment is F1, and, apart, the
census's other rows (`census`). A row's safety VCs are regenerated by Trust's
`trust-vcgen` from the MIR the stage2 compiler dumped for that row's test
(`-Ztrust-dump=mir:`); an obligation the compiler proved by R1 caller propagation
is represented by its caller-site VCs under the flipped precondition (the
formulas that proof rests on). The report directory has the harvest's provenance.

**What the test checks** (`crates/clean-olean/tests/vf4_chk_lia_f1.rs`): every
F1 obligation is `certified` or `via-r1-sites`; every certified theorem is
admitted through `ReferenceKernel::add_checked` (KR0/KR1), decided by kernel
evaluation of `chk_LIA_cases`, and the same statement flipped to `= false` is
refused as a type mismatch; the admission times give the p50/p99 R162 publishes.

**What it does not claim.** The kernel's verdict is that every listed case is
unsatisfiable (`ChkLIA.chk_LIA_cases_sound`). That the cases are the obligation's
formula in disjunctive normal form is the untrusted producer's claim; VF5's
denotation and its bridge to SemR are to prove it.
